decisions.reason: The same source message also clarifies the TTP223 touch interfaces, but a complete same-message MODIFY already records their push-pull active-HIGH outputs, R20/R25 pull-downs, and disconnected LOW state.
The button changes are a separate clause from the PIR decision and are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The PIR output and bias clarification does not change the separate panel reset interface or its EN-to-GND behavior.
The PIR sensor's push-pull output and pull-down configuration do not affect the addressable LED power, data threshold, or drive requirements.
The source confirms the electrical behavior of the separate AM312 PIR input and does not modify the sensor-board connector matrix.
Confirming a push-pull active-HIGH PIR output with a pull-down does not change the sensor-board policy for 3.3V logic compatibility or future 5V adapters.
The PIR pull-down clarification is unrelated to the SPS30 SEL-to-GND connection and I2C operating mode.
The source does not alter the e-paper backlight's switching topology, gate pull-down, PWM control, or supply selection.
The PIR electrical-interface clarification neither adds nor removes any connector in the integrated-board sensor matrix.
The PIR sensor model and input-bias semantics do not affect the LED array board's part selection, count, or layout requirements.
The PIR input clarification has no effect on the passive buzzer type or approved component policy.
The AM312 PIR input clarification concerns signal biasing and does not change the switched 5V rail, which supplies the SPS30 and ZE08 loads rather than the PIR sensor.
